eventMetadata.context_description:
**Forecast consensus for New York City on August 4, 2026, centers on a daily high near 84°F, aligning with the market’s leading 84-85°F bin at 35% implied probability.** Extended outlooks from timeanddate and similar services show an 84/69°F forecast under overcast skies with light winds around 6 mph, while seasonal guidance from the National Weather Service Climate Prediction Center favors above-average August temperatures overall.

Key differentiating factors include the strength of southerly flow advecting warmer air masses versus cloud cover and any scattered showers that could suppress peak heating. Model runs vary modestly in the extent of afternoon clearing and boundary-layer moisture, producing the spread across the 82–87°F outcomes that together hold over 80% of the probability. Sea-breeze influences and urban heat-island effects add further small-scale uncertainty for the Central Park or LaGuardia reporting stations used for resolution.

With the event less than 24 hours away, traders are weighting the most recent National Weather Service point forecasts and ensemble guidance that keep the most likely range tightly clustered around the long-term early-August normal of roughly 83°F.

**Forecast models and official outlooks position the highest temperature in New York City on August 4, 2026, near the seasonal average of 83°F at Central Park, with the market heavily favoring 84–85°F.** 

National Weather Service and extended guidance point to daytime highs in the mid- to upper-80s under partly to mostly sunny skies, consistent with the Climate Prediction Center’s 6–10 day outlook for above-normal temperatures across the Northeast during August 4–8. Warm-air advection and typical early-August solar heating support this range, while any lingering moisture or afternoon cloud build-up from recent unsettled patterns could cap readings near the lower end of the favored bins. 

Trader consensus reflects these near-term model runs and climatological context, with lower probabilities assigned to 80–83°F (cooler boundary-layer air or more clouds) and 88°F+ (stronger ridging or clearer skies than currently indicated). Updated NWS and model guidance ahead of the date will be the key drivers for any shifts in implied probabilities.

Historical climatology for early August in southern Bavaria (typical highs ~23–25 °C) underscores how anomalous the current setup is, yet ensemble spread and minor timing differences in the thermal peak keep meaningful probability on the adjacent 35 °C and 37 °C buckets. 

Traders are effectively weighting the latest short-range guidance and its uncertainty range rather than long-term averages, with further official updates from DWD or ECMWF expected to refine the precise maximum before market resolution.

Historical August baselines near 83°F provide context, yet the current pattern’s strong moisture advection and south winds of 13–15 mph introduce measurable uncertainty that traders have priced across multiple outcomes rather than converging on a single bin. Updated model runs and real-time observations from the National Weather Service will likely refine these ranges as the day progresses.

Typical early-August daytime highs average near 30–31 °C under the influence of the subtropical ridge, with the urban heat-island effect and high humidity (often >70 %) amplifying perceived warmth; however, the market focuses on official thermometer readings. Short-range ensemble guidance for 4–6 August shows a narrow spread centered on 29–32 °C, with the majority of solutions clustering at 30 °C, directly supporting the 39 % market-implied probability for that outcome and the secondary weight on 31 °C. Minor model spread and the possibility of localized cloud cover or a weak frontal passage keep lower values (29 °C) viable at 16.5 %, while the low odds assigned to 33 °C or higher reflect limited intensification potential before the next forecast update.
